$$
\prod_{i=1}^{\text{pos} - 1} (m - i) = (m - 1)(m - 2)(m - 3) \cdots (m - (\text{pos} - 1))
$$

This is a product of $ \text{pos} - 1 $ consecutive integers starting from $ m - 1 $ and decreasing by 1 each time.

This expression is equivalent to the **falling factorial**, which can be written in terms of factorials as:

$$
\prod_{i=1}^{\text{pos} - 1} (m - i) = \frac{(m - 1)!}{(m - \text{pos})!}
$$

### Explanation:

- The numerator $(m - 1)!$ represents the product of all integers from 1 to $m - 1$.
- The denominator $(m - \text{pos})!$ cancels out the terms from $m - \text{pos}$ to 1, leaving only the product from $m - 1$ down to $m - (\text{pos} - 1)$, which is exactly the desired product.

$$

$$
